clue.text: Fairies going to hospital to die

parts.note: peris are fairy-like spirits of Persian legend
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Little fairy folk taken to hospital to breathe their last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to' simply places the second piece after the first. PERI is a crossword favourite for a fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to lose one's life, a common formal synonym for dying.

clue.text: Declare academic has no alternative

indicators.note: has no says a word is missing from the academic's title

parts.note: a professor is a senior academic
or is the word offering an alternative

explanation.surface: An academic announces that there is no other option.
explanation.definitionFit: To profess is to state openly or affirm a belief, as in professing one's faith.

clue.text: Bolt taking top off shrub

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed from the hedge plant

parts.note: privet is a common hedging shrub

explanation.surface: Someone bolts after pruning the top of a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' tempts as running away; it is the metal fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin used to fasten plates together, much like a bolt.

clue.text: God of the French in the cavity

indicators.note: in places the French article inside the word for a cavity

parts.note: a sinus is a cavity in the skull
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A deity of the French hidden in a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Silenus is the drunken old woodland deity of Greek myth, companion and tutor of Dionysus.

clue.text: I live by a sunken valley in part of Europe

parts.note: taken as written
to be is to exist or live
a ria is a river valley drowned by the sea

explanation.surface: Someone describes their home beside a flooded valley somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just sets the pieces side by side. Ria is a geography term, common in crosswords, for a drowned river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal, a region in the south-west corner of the continent.

clue.text: Hard man from Uruguay is interrupting literary uncle's brother

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the pair goes inside the brother's title

parts.note: Brer, as in Brer Rabbit, is how the brothers are styled in Uncle Remus stories
U is a short abbreviation for Uruguay
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tough guy from South America barges in on a character from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Remus is the narrator of Joel Chandler Harris's folk tales, where animals are Brer (brother) Rabbit, Brer Fox and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruiser is a big, aggressive, tough man, someone who enjoys fighting.

clue.text: Place bet on "Fiddler''s Wax", an unpromising horse

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the stake word follows the wax word

parts.note: violinists rub rosin on their bows
an ante is a stake put down before play in poker

explanation.surface: A punter backs a horse named Fiddler's Wax, which looks a poor prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the bet after the wax.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosinante is Don Quixote's bony old nag, and the name is used for any broken-down worn-out steed.

clue.text: Mental blank rendering travelling men incontinent?

indicators.note: split as two words, its opening in puts the moved letters inside the landmass that follows

parts.note: Asia is the largest continent

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of the males shift position

parts.note: the letters to be moved

explanation.surface: A memory lapse that leaves travelling men unable to control their bladders.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'incontinent' as 'in continent': the men, rearranged, are put inside ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, leaving the mind empty of what it once held.

clue.text: Penny Black in German river turned to stone

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny

indicators.note: turned, in a down clue, means the river's name runs upwards
in places the colour abbreviation inside the river's name

parts.note: the Elbe flows through Germany
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A famous old stamp, the Penny Black, sinks in a German river and turns to stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Penny Black was the world's first postage stamp, issued in Britain in 1840.
explanation.definitionFit: A pebble is a small smooth stone, worn round by water.

clue.text: "Small Helpings", a book about universal currency, is in verse

indicators.note: about means going around, so the book's word wraps round the next item

parts.note: a novel is a book of fiction
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair inside the word for verse

parts.note: a line is a single row of verse
the ecu was the European currency unit before the euro
taken as written

explanation.surface: A title in quotes, apparently a poetic book about a worldwide currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers run side by side. 'Small Helpings' in quotes poses as a book title, but it is the definition. The ecu was Europe's accounting currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouvelle cuisine is the light modern style of cooking famous for serving tiny portions artfully arranged on large plates.

clue.text: Congress takes on heavyweight churchman

parts.note: congress is an old word for sexual intercourse
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A political assembly squares up to a heavyweight figure of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' reads as a parliament, but here it is the other, intimate sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer who looks after the building and graveyard, so a churchman of a humble kind.

clue.text: Geometrical proportions in transport company

indicators.note: in puts the mathematical ratios inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a bus is public transport
sines are trigonometric ratios of a triangle's sides

explanation.surface: Mathematical ratios turn up somewhere in a transport firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A business is a commercial firm or enterprise, the same thing as a trading company.

clue.text: Drawing of ship replacing recipe in lads' magazine

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter is swapped out for another in the magazine's name

parts.note: Esquire is a men's lifestyle magazine
SS stands for steamship
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An illustration of a ship appears in place of a recipe in a men's magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe (Latin 'take') heads old prescriptions. Swap it out of ESQUIRE for SS.
explanation.definitionFit: An esquisse is a rough preliminary sketch, a French art term for a first draft drawing.

clue.text: Lifeline to Mum losing head and feeling sick when carbon replaces oxygen

indicators.note: replaces says one element's symbol is swapped in for another's in the word for queasy
losing head means the first letter of the mother word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before its first letter goes
bilious means nauseous
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A sick, beheaded mother and some chemistry: a jumble of medical scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: UM from Mum, then BILIOUS with C for O gives BILICUS. 'Lifeline' is fair because the navel marks the cord that fed the unborn child.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbilicus, or navel, is where the umbilical cord, an unborn baby's supply line, was attached.

clue.text: Fugitive lacking a point of departure

indicators.note: lacking means something is missing, so a letter is dropped from the word for fugitive

parts.note: a runaway is someone who has fled
taken as written

explanation.surface: An escapee with nowhere to start from.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft takes off from the strip of tarmac at an airport, so it is where flights depart.

clue.text: Help back, carrying a good bundle of leaves

indicators.note: back says the word for help is read from right to left
carrying means holding something inside, so the reversed word takes in a letter

parts.note: to abet is to help
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone helping out while carrying a good bundle of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter for 'a' goes inside the reversed help word just after its second letter, and G for good is tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea bag is a small porous sachet of dried tea leaves for brewing, so literally a packet of leaves.

clue.text: Without hesitation, perimeter can be made less populous

indicators.note: can be made says the remaining letters are fashioned into something new
without means lacking, so a sound of hesitation is taken out of the boundary word

parts.note: the letters to work on
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Decisively, a boundary can be thinned of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptier means holding fewer people or things, so a place that is more empty has fewer inhabitants.

clue.text: Traditional subject getting right into Greek character and Roman leader

indicators.note: getting ... into says the first item is placed inside the Greek letter

parts.note: gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: leader is the first letter, the one at the front

parts.note: first letter of Roman

explanation.surface: A classical education: Greek characters and a Roman general.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar was the core of the old schooling, so it is the classic subject taught in grammar schools.

clue.text: Form of bribery involving plate of fruit

indicators.note: involving means including, so the reshaped word takes in an extra letter
a form of something is a version in another shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
an L-plate shows a learner driver, giving L

explanation.surface: Some kind of corruption involving a plate of fruit, like a bribe served at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates are the red L signs British learner drivers must show on their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The bilberry is a small dark blue berry of moorland shrubs, related to the blueberry.

clue.text: Back without king of northwest France?

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the backing phrase goes round the royal letter

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A cry to retreat without the monarch, set in north-west France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, so one wants to remove K; it means outside here. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Breton describes things from Brittany, the peninsula region in the far north-west of France.

clue.text: Nothing, on reflection, to chuckle about, losing tip of tongue

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word for nothing is flipped

parts.note: nil means nothing

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for chuckle is read backwards
losing tip drops the end letter of the reversed chuckle

parts.note: to chuckle is to laugh

explanation.surface: Nothing to laugh about when you bite the tip of your tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip of tongue' is not a letter selection: 'losing tip' is the instruction and 'of tongue' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingual is the adjective relating to the tongue, from Latin lingua.

clue.text: Queen's introduced to pugilist's garden feature

indicators.note: introduced to means brought into, so the queen's letters go inside the boxer's name

parts.note: Rocky Balboa is the boxer of the Rocky films
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: The Queen meets a boxer in his garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is a garden bed built of stones with alpine plants growing between them.

clue.text: Sack for disrupting oil flow outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for flow sits around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a spate is a sudden flood or flow

indicators.note: disrupting throws things into disorder, so the letters of the fuel are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is fired for interrupting the flow of oil, as at a pipeline or refinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismissal from a job, but it is the verb meaning to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoliate is to pillage or plunder, just as an army sacks a captured town.

clue.text: A sign of resignation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a posted announcement or placard
second meaning: formal warning that one is leaving a job

explanation.surface: A gesture that shows someone has given up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resignation' reads as weary acceptance, but it means quitting a job: one hands in one's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice is a displayed board with information, and giving notice is formally announcing that you are leaving employment.

clue.text: Vagrant gin-drinking Frenchman

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the snare word swallows the Frenchman's letter

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals
M is short for monsieur

explanation.surface: A homeless Frenchman with a bottle of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the spirit; it is the old word for an animal snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless person wandering from place to place, a vagrant.

clue.text: Confused flower bearing the dead to "The Band From Hell"

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the flower word holds the dead word inside it

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, and Dante's city of Hell
a combo is a small band of musicians
a bud is a flower not yet open
the late are those who have died

explanation.surface: Mourners carry flowers to a gig by a heavy-metal outfit called The Band From Hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' tempts as a river, but here it is a bloom. Read 'The Band From Hell' as Hell's band, DIS COMBO, which leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Discombobulated is a jokey word for thoroughly disconcerted or bewildered, a fancy synonym for muddled.

clue.text: A redhead wearing pink beads

indicators.note: wearing puts the colour word around the pair like a garment

parts.note: rosy is pink in colour
taken as written
the head, or first letter, of red

explanation.surface: A red-haired woman dressed in pink, with a string of beads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' reads as a ginger person but simply means the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a string of prayer beads used by Catholics to count devotions.

clue.text: Not a popular success — pasty, gutless and flaccid

parts.note: a flop is a failure with the public

indicators.note: gutless means with the insides removed, so only the outer letters of the word stay

parts.note: first and last letters of pasty

explanation.surface: A description of a feeble man: unsuccessful, pale, cowardly and limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like a pale complexion, or a Cornish pie, but only its two ends are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Floppy describes something limp and hanging loosely, lacking firmness, which is what flaccid means.
